findings.title: Successful cleanup batches are logged as errors
findings.body: The new cleanup paths emit Error logs for every successful SELECT and DELETE, including empty batches, with a nil error. Orphan-tag cleanup runs even when annotation retention is disabled, so normal scheduled cleanup now produces recurring false error reports. This can trigger log-based alerts and obscure actual failures; log successful operations at Debug level and reserve Error for failures.

findings.title: Build the SQLite ID list without repeatedly copying its entire prefix
findings.body: For SQLite batches above 999, each iteration formats the entire accumulated ID list into a new string. Building a batch of N IDs therefore takes quadratic copying and allocation rather than linear work. Configured batches containing tens of thousands of IDs can allocate gigabytes of temporary strings, causing substantial GC pressure and delaying cleanup and other work. Use strings.Builder or a byte buffer to append each ID once.

findings.title: Bound parameterized deletes by the database parameter limit
findings.body: The non-SQLite branch creates one bound parameter per selected ID without capping the batch. MySQL prepared statements and PostgreSQL's parameter protocol support at most 65,535 parameters, so an annotation cleanup batch configured above that limit fails whenever enough eligible rows exist. The previous subquery-based DELETE did not have this restriction. Split the selected IDs into supported-size deletes or otherwise avoid exceeding the backend's parameter limit.

findings.title: Keep the shared cleanup cadence unchanged
findings.body: Changing this ticker from ten minutes to one minute accelerates every cleanup job, not just annotation cleanup. Temporary-file directory scans, snapshot and dashboard-version deletion, image cleanup, invite expiration, and query-history retention now run ten times as often, increasing filesystem and database load independently of the deadlock fix. The shared cleanup timeout is still nine minutes, so slow cleanup passes can also leave a tick pending and run again immediately. Keep the existing cadence unless this broader scheduling change is separately justified.
